Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches. This is a REWORK round on SFCC-91. The affected file is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` — the SIBLING ATOM (Step 2, already committed as `ab04241`), NOT the molecule from Step 3. Do not stage, do not commit. Do not touch any other file.

Marcel opened the `KeyboardNavigation` story for `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` in real Storybook and reported: focusing the first swatch ("Bay Blue") shows a focus outline box whose RIGHT edge is broken/missing — the top and bottom lines appear to terminate partway across rather than closing into a complete rectangle, and there's no visible right vertical edge at all. A screenshot confirms this precisely: a box with a clear left edge, top/bottom edges that cut off partway, and no right edge.

## Investigate first — confirm or refute this hypothesis with a REAL browser render before fixing anything

The atom's recipe (`zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`) currently has:
```ts
_focusVisible: {
  outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
  outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
},
```
`outline` with a positive `outlineOffset` draws OUTSIDE the element's own border box. The swatches sit with `gap: 0` in the parent group (confirmed correct per Figma — swatches are meant to be flush against each other). My hypothesis: because swatches have zero gap, the swatch immediately to the RIGHT of a focused one sits with its own background fill starting exactly where the focused swatch's outline needs to extend outward into. In normal document flow with no `z-index`/stacking context on either element, a later sibling paints on top of an earlier one — so the next swatch's background would paint directly over the right (and possibly top-right/bottom-right corner) portion of the focused swatch's outward-extending outline, exactly matching the reported symptom. This would mean ANY swatch with a sibling immediately to its right (i.e. every swatch except the last one in a row) has this same bug — only the last swatch in any row could show a complete, uncovered outline.

**Confirm this empirically using Playwright/real Chromium** (already used successfully in earlier rounds of this build to prove a similar computed-style issue) — do not just reason about it:
1. Render `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` (or directly render 2+ `ZimmColourSwatch` instances side by side with zero gap, matching how the molecule composes them) with real Chakra theme + real `--zimm-*` CSS variables injected (check how `zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx` and prior rounds' Playwright investigations set this up — there's established precedent in this codebase/session for this exact setup).
2. Programmatically focus the FIRST swatch (matching what the `KeyboardNavigation` story's `play` function does).
3. Take a real screenshot and/or read the actual paint/stacking behavior (e.g. via `page.evaluate` reading `getBoundingClientRect()` of both the outline's expected extent and confirming visually or via element z-ordering that the next sibling covers it) to confirm the outline is genuinely being covered, and specifically that it's the SECOND swatch's own box causing it (not something else — e.g. rule out `overflow: hidden` on a parent, rule out the outline not rendering at all due to some other bug).
4. Also render and focus the LAST swatch in the row (nothing to its right) and confirm — per the hypothesis — that ITS outline shows completely, with no missing edge, since it has no sibling to its right. This is the key differential test: if only non-last swatches show the bug and the last one is fine, that strongly confirms the sibling-paint-order theory rather than some other cause.

Report your actual findings from this real-browser investigation BEFORE describing your fix — if the hypothesis is wrong, or only partially right, say so and adjust the fix accordingly rather than applying the below blindly.

## If confirmed — the fix

Standard, well-established CSS pattern for exactly this "adjacent zero-gap sibling covers an outward outline" problem: lift the focused element above its siblings in paint order, scoped only to the focus-visible state so it never affects normal (unfocused) layout or z-ordering:

```ts
_focusVisible: {
  position: 'relative',
  zIndex: 1,
  outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
  outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
},
```

`position: 'relative'` is required for `zIndex` to have any effect (a `static`-positioned element ignores `z-index` entirely per CSS spec) — without it, adding `zIndex` alone would do nothing, which would be an easy, silent way to ship a fix that doesn't actually work; make sure you understand why both are needed together, not just copy them. This must be scoped inside `_focusVisible` only, not applied unconditionally to the `swatch` part's base styles — an always-on `position: relative` would be harmless here but is unnecessary scope creep, and always-on `zIndex` could have unintended effects on unrelated stacking elsewhere on a real PDP (e.g. against a header dropdown or modal later composed on the same page) that a scoped, state-only application avoids entirely.

**Prove the fix actually works with the same real-browser method, not just applying it and assuming.** Re-run your Playwright investigation with the fix applied: focus the first swatch again, confirm the outline's right edge is now fully visible and un-covered by the next sibling. Take a real before/after comparison (screenshot or precise computed-geometry check) and report both.

## What NOT to do

Do not touch `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/` (Step 3, currently mid-rework on a separate, unrelated pair of fixes in a parallel track — touching it risks a merge/scope conflict). Do not touch anything in `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` (Step 1, committed). Do not touch `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` (Tier 1). Do not change anything else about the atom's recipe — the `selected` bottom-border logic, the container geometry, the background token — all of that was independently verified correct twice already in Step 2's own review rounds.

## Verification — run yourself, report exact output

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx
npm run test
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Baselines: tsc 0 errors; the atom's own scoped test file currently 8/8 passing (this fix shouldn't need a new test necessarily, since it's a pure CSS-property addition inside an existing recipe branch, but if you judge a regression test is cheap and valuable here — e.g. asserting `position`/`zIndex` resolve correctly under `_focusVisible` via `getComputedStyle` after a real focus event — add one; your call, but if you skip it, say why); full suite before this round; lint/audit:tokens unchanged, none in this atom's files.

Report back: your real-browser confirmation of the root cause (with actual observed evidence, not just "confirmed"), the exact fix applied, and your real-browser proof that the fix resolves it — both the "before" (broken) and "after" (fixed) states, observed directly, not assumed.

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe for a single PDP colour swatch — a clickable rectangle filled with that colour
5	 * variation's product photo. Two parts: `swatch` is the outer clickable box (geometry,
6	 * background, border, focus ring); `image` is the element carrying the dynamic
7	 * background-image fill — the URL itself cannot live here, see the component's own comment on
8	 * why that one `__css` spread stays dynamic.
9	 *
10	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for the three states this recipe distinguishes, not
11	 * estimated from surrounding metadata — Unselected (node 40000307:13826), Selected
12	 * (40000307:13831), Focus (40002689:3839), all under `size=Large/Rectangle`.
13	 */
14	export const ZimmColourSwatch = {
15	  parts: ['swatch', 'image'],
16	
17	  baseStyle: ({ selected }: { selected?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
18	    swatch: {
19	      display: 'inline-block',
20	      cursor: 'pointer',
21	      // Figma's Rectangle width (48px). Height (72px) has no direct token — the named scale has
22	      // nothing between 64px and 140px — so it's expressed as an aspect ratio on the width
23	      // instead. 2:3, not the incidentally different ratio Figma's raw code-gen attached to the
24	      // placeholder product photo pasted into that frame instance: the Selected-state node
25	      // carries its own dev annotation reading "Image aspect ratio - 2:3", which is the number
26	      // to trust here.
27	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)',
28	      aspectRatio: '2 / 3',
29	      // Identical across Unselected/Selected/Focus — ivory[200] / background['02'] in
30	      // theme/foundation/colour.ts.
31	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-02)',
32	      // Selected: a bottom-only border — the raw Figma export is unambiguous, a `border-b`
33	      // utility rather than a full box border. Colour is grey[900] / border.focus, the only
34	      // alias-tier value that resolves to it (border.default and border.secondary are both
35	      // light greys and never appear anywhere in this design).
36	      ...(selected
37	        ? {
38	            borderBottomWidth: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)',
39	            borderBottomStyle: 'solid',
40	            borderBottomColor: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
41	          }
42	        : {}),
43	      // Focus: Figma draws this as the Selected baseline plus a ring at slightly asymmetric
44	      // per-side offsets, same colour. Not replicated literally — there is no other precedent
45	      // anywhere in this codebase for a non-uniform ring, and the asymmetry reads as that one
46	      // frame instance's export noise rather than a deliberate design decision. Mirrors
47	      // zimmNavItem.css.ts's own focus-ring block instead: a uniform `outline` + `outlineOffset`
48	      // pair, applied independently of `selected` above — a swatch can be focused without being
49	      // selected, and selected without being focused. `--zimm-focus-ring` already composites the
50	      // same border-width/colour pair used above; `--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default` matches
51	      // three of Figma's four side offsets.
52	      _focusVisible: {
53	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
54	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
55	      },
56	    },
57	    image: {
58	      display: 'block',
59	      width: '100%',
60	      height: '100%',
61	      backgroundSize: 'cover',
62	      backgroundPosition: 'center',
63	      backgroundRepeat: 'no-repeat',
64	    },
65	  }),
66	};

3	/**
4	 * Recipe for the PDP colour-swatch group — the "Colour: Bay Blue" label row, and (when there is
5	 * more than one populated colour) the row of ZimmColourSwatch rectangles beneath it. This recipe
6	 * only lays the group out; each swatch's own fill/border/focus styling stays in the sibling
7	 * ZimmColourSwatch atom's own recipe.
8	 *
9	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for this exact component, not estimated — node
10	 * 40000307:13867 ("ColourOptions"), within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026.
11	 *
12	 * Six parts:
13	 *   - `root` — outer vertical flex container: the label row above, the swatches row below.
14	 *   - `label` — the label row ("labelContainer" in Figma): the label-group (the two
15	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component
16	 *     itself, not a seventh part here; see index.tsx's own comment for why) plus the pagination
17	 *     controls, right-aligned purely via the label-group's own `flex: 1 0 0` rather than an
18	 *     absolute-position hack.
19	 *   - `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text specifically (e.g. "Bay Blue"). Gets its own
20	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
21	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
22	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).
23	 *   - `swatches` — the horizontal row of rendered ZimmColourSwatch children. Once paginated
24	 *     (`isPaginated`), reserves a fixed page-width footprint regardless of how many items the
25	 *     current window actually renders — see its own baseStyle comment below for the layout bug
26	 *     this prevents.
27	 *   - `pagination` — wrapper around the two chevron buttons.
28	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).
29	 */
30	
31	/**
32	 * Matches `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` in this component's own index.tsx (Figma's own interaction
33	 * annotation: "Pagination appears if there are more than 4 swatches"). Kept as its own literal
34	 * here rather than imported across files — this recipe stays a self-contained, co-located file,
35	 * the same precedent the sibling zimmColourSwatch.css.ts already sets for a state-dependent
36	 * baseStyle function. If `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` in index.tsx ever changes, update this to match.
37	 */
38	const PAGE_SIZE = 4;
39	
40	/**
41	 * A full page's reserved width: PAGE_SIZE swatches at the atom's own fixed 48px width
42	 * (`--zimm-scale-1200` — see zimmColourSwatch.css.ts's `swatch.width`), with no per-swatch gap
43	 * (`swatches.gap` below is 0, same as the atom's own adjacency). Applied only once paginated —
44	 * see the `swatches` part below.
45	 */
46	const PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH = `calc(${PAGE_SIZE} * var(--zimm-scale-1200))`;
47	
48	export const ZimmColourSwatchGroup = {
49	  parts: ['root', 'label', 'labelName', 'swatches', 'pagination', 'pageButton'],
50	
51	  baseStyle: ({ isPaginated }: { isPaginated?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
52	    root: {
53	      display: 'flex',
54	      flexDirection: 'column',
55	      // 8px between the label row and the swatches row. No background here — background lives
56	      // per-swatch, already handled by the atom's own recipe.
57	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
58	    },
59	
60	    label: {
61	      display: 'flex',
62	      alignItems: 'center',
63	      // 24px. Matches spacing.xl exactly, so the named step is used rather than the numerically
64	      // identical --zimm-scale-600 alias — see bottomBar.css.ts's own `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`
65	      // usage for the same 24px value elsewhere in this codebase.
66	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
67	      // 8px between the label-group and the pagination controls.
68	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
69	    },
70	
71	    labelName: {
72	      textStyle: 'caption',
73	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
74	      // The truncating half of the label-group's two text pieces (the static "Colour:" text
75	      // beside it never truncates — see index.tsx). `flex: 1 0 0` lets it consume the
76	      // label-group's remaining width; `minWidth: 0` is required for a flex item to actually
77	      // shrink below its content size instead of overflowing; the rest is the standard
78	      // single-line-ellipsis triad.
79	      flex: '1 0 0',
80	      minWidth: 0,
81	      overflow: 'hidden',
82	      textOverflow: 'ellipsis',
83	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
84	    },
85	
86	    swatches: {
87	      display: 'flex',
88	      // Non-paginated (<= SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours): sizes naturally to however many
89	      // swatches are actually present. Unchanged, deliberately out of scope for this fix — there
90	      // is no confirmed design value either way for a 2- or 3-colour row's width, so nothing was
91	      // invented here.
92	      //
93	      // Paginated (> SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours, windowed to a fixed PAGE_SIZE-wide
94	      // slice per page): a plain `100%` here resolves against `root`'s own width — but `root` has
95	      // no explicit width of its own, so it auto-fits to its widest child, which is this very
96	      // element. That circular relationship meant the *rendered* width tracked how many items the
97	      // current window actually held (192px for a full 4-item page, 96px for a 2-item final
98	      // page), so `root` — and `label` above it, itself 100% of that same `root` — visibly
99	      // resized between pages. Confirmed directly in a running Storybook: the pagination chevrons
100	      // jumped position between the two pages of the `Paginated` story. Reserving
101	      // PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH regardless of the current page's real item count breaks that
102	      // loop — the footprint stays constant across every page, full or partial. A partial final
103	      // page's unused space simply remains empty to the right: the flex default
104	      // `justify-content: flex-start` already left-aligns the rendered items, so nothing further
105	      // is needed for that.
106	      width: isPaginated ? PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH : '100%',
107	      ...(isPaginated ? { minWidth: PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH } : {}),
108	      // Confirmed directly off the Figma export, not a stylistic default: the 4-swatch example
109	      // measures exactly 192px total width for four 48px-wide swatches (4 x 48, no gap
110	      // contribution) — swatches sit directly adjacent. Do not add a gap here; that would be a
111	      // real deviation from the design, not a stylistic default.
112	      gap: 0,
113	    },
114	
115	    pagination: {
116	      display: 'flex',
117	      alignItems: 'center',
118	      // No inter-button gap value exists in the Figma export handed to this step — left at the
119	      // flex default (no `gap` declared at all) rather than invented. Revisit if a designer
120	      // confirms a real value.
121	    },
122	
123	    pageButton: {
124	      display: 'flex',
125	      alignItems: 'center',
126	      justifyContent: 'center',
127	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
128	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
129	      // Resets the native <button> UA chrome so the box is exactly the 24x24 the design calls
130	      // for, with the 16px ZimmIcon centred inside it by the flex alignment above.
131	      padding: 0,
132	      border: 'none',
133	      background: 'none',
134	      cursor: 'pointer',
135	      // No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control — same "leave an
136	      // unspecified visual state alone rather than invent one" precedent as swatch-group's own
137	      // disabled colour logic (see this codebase's Known Gaps notes). The native `disabled`
138	      // attribute (set in index.tsx) already makes the control genuinely inert and announces as
139	      // disabled to assistive tech; only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX
140	      // keyword, not a design token.
141	      _disabled: {
142	        cursor: 'not-allowed',
143	      },
144	      // Same uniform ring every other interactive control in ui-kits/ uses (zimmColourSwatch,
145	      // zimmNavItem) — --zimm-focus-ring already composites the border-width/colour pair.
146	      _focusVisible: {
147	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
148	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
149	      },
150	    },
151	  }),
152	};

## Investigation — real Chromium, not reasoning-only

I built a byte-accurate reproduction outside the repo (`/tmp`, cleaned up afterward — see Deviations below) rather than trusting a mental model of CSS paint order:

- **Real token values**, not hand-transcribed: bundled the actual `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` via esbuild and executed it to get the real derived strings — `--zimm-focus-ring: "1px solid #191919"`, `--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default: "2px"`, `--zimm-color-bg-02: "#f6f4f1"`, `--zimm-scale-1200: "48px"`.
- **Real layout composition**: a `display:flex; gap:0` row of 48×72px swatches, matching `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`'s `swatches` part exactly (confirmed by reading that file — read-only, not modified).
- **Real focus interaction**: a verbatim port of the molecule's own `handleSwatchesKeyDown` roving-focus logic, driven by real `page.keyboard.press('Tab'/'ArrowRight')` key events (not synthetic `.focus()` calls) so `:focus-visible` modality matches the way a real keyboard user would trigger it.
- Ran via Playwright's own bundled Chromium (v148, launched as a local subprocess — no network dependency, confirmed working).

**Root cause — confirmed, not assumed.** Screenshots (`deviceScaleFactor: 4` for pixel-level clarity) of the first swatch ("Bay Blue") focused, current recipe:

- Clear left edge, top/bottom edges terminating partway across, **no right edge at all** — pixel-for-pixel identical to Marcel's reported screenshot.
- `getBoundingClientRect`/`elementFromPoint` confirmed *why*: sampling the exact pixel where the outline's right-edge ring should paint (`rect.right + outlineOffset + outlineWidth/2`) returns the **next sibling swatch**, not the focused one — a real, opaque, later-painted box occupying that space. The mirror sample on the left (nothing adjacent) returns the page background, not an element — consistent with the intact left edge.
- **Differential control test**, focusing the *last* swatch (no right-hand sibling): screenshot shows a **complete, uncovered rectangle** — all four edges intact. This isolates the cause to exactly "has a sibling to the right," matching the hypothesis precisely.

One honest caveat on methodology: `elementFromPoint` alone can't distinguish "outline hidden" from "outline visible but not hit-testable" (CSS outlines never participate in hit-testing, in any variant) — so that signal only proves the *structural setup* (an opaque sibling box sits exactly where the ring needs to render). The actual visible-or-not determination came from reading the screenshots directly (multimodal), the same way Marcel confirmed it.

**A nuance worth flagging honestly.** I also ran a third, diagnostic-only variant (`z-index: 1` alone, no `position` change) to test the claim "without position:relative, z-index does nothing." In real Chromium, that variant's screenshot was **also** a complete rectangle — because a `swatch` is a direct flex item of `swatches`, and the Flexbox spec has a documented carve-out: *"z-index values other than auto create a stacking context even if position is static."* So in this specific flex-item context, `z-index` alone was empirically sufficient. This doesn't make the prescribed fix wrong — `position: relative` is harmless (no offset is set, so it doesn't move the box) and makes the rule correct even if `swatch` is ever composed outside a flex parent, rather than depending on a layout detail owned by a sibling file. I applied the fix exactly as instructed and documented this nuance in the code comment rather than restating the imprecise general claim as if I hadn't checked it.

## Fix applied

**File:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`

```ts

  position: 'relative',
  zIndex: 1,
  outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
  outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
},
```

Plus a comment explaining the mechanism and the flex-item nuance above, for future maintainers.

**Proof the fix works, same real-browser method:** re-ran the identical Playwright script against the fixed recipe values (also re-extracted, post-edit, directly from the real edited `.css.ts` file via esbuild — not retyped by hand — confirming the shipped object is exactly `{position: "relative", zIndex: 1, outline: "var(--zimm-focus-ring)", outlineOffset: "var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)"}`). Screenshots after the fix: first swatch focused → complete rectangle, all four edges intact; last swatch focused → still a complete rectangle (no regression).

## Regression test — judgment call: not added, with evidence

I probed this directly rather than guessing: rendered the real component under `ChakraProvider`, called `.focus()`, and checked `swatch.matches(':focus-visible')` and `getComputedStyle`. Result: **jsdom does not match `:focus-visible` at all** — `matches(':focus-visible')` returned `false`, and `getComputedStyle` showed `position: static`, `zIndex: auto`, `outlineStyle: none` even though a real DOM focus had occurred. A jsdom-based regression test for `position`/`zIndex` under `_focusVisible` would therefore be vacuous (it can't be made to fail on a real regression), so I skipped it rather than add a test that looks like coverage but isn't.
